lessonTitle: Differences between Medical, Commercial, Market Access and R&D

slides.title: Confusing These Roles Damages MSL Credibility
bullets: Four functions touch a medicine at different points in its life
Confusing their roles is one of the fastest ways to lose credibility
Knowing the precise boundaries enables compliant, effective work

slides.title: R&D Builds the Foundation Everyone Uses
bullets: Designs and runs the pivotal clinical trials
Defines the Target Product Profile
Hands off a medicine with a regulator-approved label
Longest time horizon; the dossier becomes everyone else's foundation

slides.title: Medical Affairs Translates the Dossier Into Real-World Value
bullets: Interprets the evidence for practising clinicians
Generates post-approval evidence: RWE, registries, investigator studies
Maintains scientific exchange independent of sales targets
McKinsey: a strategic pillar, not an interface or compliance buffer

slides.title: Market Access Builds the Economic Case
bullets: Sits between the science and the health system's economics
Builds pricing, reimbursement and health-economic value propositions
Persuades payers, HTA bodies and hospital formularies
Uses clinical and real-world evidence Medical Affairs often helped generate

slides.title: Commercial Owns the Promotional Relationship
bullets: Sales representatives communicate approved, on-label messages
Goal: drive appropriate use and volume
Commercial's conversations are promotional by design and regulation
Medical Affairs' conversations must never be

slides.title: Governance Controls Protect Medical Independence
bullets: Separate reporting lines, restricted data sharing, documented rules of engagement
HHS OIG guidance: keep "a respectful distance" from sales and marketing
Sharing prescriber-level insights for sales targeting is a genuine compliance risk

slides.title: Know Which Conversation Belongs to Which Function
bullets: Redirect commercial questions to the right colleague
Protect the independence that makes your scientific input credible
Your job is knowing exactly where each function's line sits

takeaway.title: Medical Affairs sits structurally apart from R&D, Market Access and Commercial, and the firewall protecting that separation is non-negotiable
bullets: R&D builds the evidence base; Medical Affairs translates it into scientific value
Market Access monetizes evidence; Commercial promotes on-label messages
A protected firewall keeps Medical Affairs' exchange free of sales influence
